By Judi Franco ,
2 hours ago I love making things. Resin, jewelry, gifts, random projects that start with ‚Äúthis seems easy‚Äù and end with glitter everywhere. So when I heard that The Craft Room reopened in Washington Township in a brand-new space, I got genuinely excited. And honestly, we need more places like this.
This is one of those places that NJ should be proud to have. It represents the creativity and the industriousness of our residents. And it‚Äôs really something to be proud of. And its grand reopening really takes the idea to the next level.
Upstairs is unreal. It‚Äôs like a really good craft fair, except it‚Äôs open all the time. There you‚Äôll find a marketplace filled with handmade items of the best quality. Everything from home decor to jewelry to gifts and creative pieces from more than 25 talented local artists.
Canva / Townsquare Media illustration SEE MORE: New study: NJ is the fifth most stressed state. Here‚Äôs why Downstairs gets even cooler with its DIY Workshop. Here, you pick a project, they give you all the supplies and instructions, and you actually get to make something. It‚Äôs the kind of thing you‚Äôll want to do for a special birthday, a girls night out, or just something cool you‚Äôve never experienced before.
They‚Äôre already booking workshops and parties for 2026, and they also do beautiful custom paper goods for weddings and events.
And to top it off. even have a big backyard with plans for future events, plus the entire space is handicap accessible, including the downstairs studio and bathroom.
This isn‚Äôt just a store. It‚Äôs a creative hub. You can shop handmade items, take classes, host parties, or even sell your own creations there.
As a crafter, I love this idea. As a Jersey girl, I love seeing small businesses like this thrive.
If you‚Äôre anywhere near Washington Township, this is absolutely worth checking out. Come to think of it, it‚Äôs actually with the drive even if you‚Äôre no where near there. We need more of this is New Jersey

NJ towns that need to build the most affordable housing These 33 municipalities have the greatest number of affordable housing units that should be built, according to calculations by the Department of Community Affairs.
The "present need" refers to existing but deficient housing occupied by low- and moderate-income households. "Prospective need" refers to the housing that would have to be built in the next 10 years to accommodate the estimated growth of low- and moderate-income households. The state used a formula that considers a municipality's income and land capacity.
The current housing and population counts are from the 2020 Census. An amazing NJ restaurant in a historic building If you've never been to Lambertville, you're really missing out on a true gem of a town in New Jersey.
And if you've never been to Lambertville Station you're missing out on a really great restaurant in a truly historic building.
It's housed in the building that acted as the Lambertville train station dating back to 1867.
The building and the town went through its tough times, but for the last 40 years, Lambertville Station has been serving diners in a casual upscale atmosphere with excellent food.
Last year a prominent restaurant group called Genesis Hospitality took over the historic dining spot and they've continued the excellence that has made this place a must-go-to spot anytime you're in town.
The menu consists of varied contemporary American favorites with plenty of options.
The food and the service are excellent and are a good fit for couples, families, and special occasions.
There is a first-class Inn on the property on the river across the parking lot if you want to stay over. Gallery Credit: Dennis Malloy Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media If you've walking over from Pennsylvania over the New Hope-Lambertville Bridge, it's right at the end of the bridge. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media You can see the Lambertville Inn clearly from the PA side of the river and the bridge. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media The building makes a great first impression coming into New Jersey. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media You can go through the main entrance or head straight for the pub and wine bar. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media The old ticket booth acts as the hostess station. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media There are two tiers of dining indoors along the old railroad tracks. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media If you're just interested in having a few cocktails instead of lunch or dinner head downstairs. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media Their wine cellar pub is one of the most inviting coziest lounges anywhere. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media If you prefer to dine outside, the heaters keep things comfortable well into the cooler weather. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media No worries, the train tracks aren't in use anymore. Dennis Malloy/ Townsquare Media If you want to walk off your meal the towpath behind the restaurant is a perfect quiet spot. Dennis Malloy/Townsquare Media From any perspective the Lambertville Inn is the perfect choice for any meal anytime.
